chapter: The Second Herd and its sidemen
title: Neal Hefti and Shorty Rogers as writers for the band
summary: Hefti wrote few full arrangements but contributed head ideas and fixes; Shorty Rogers also wrote good things for the band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You had -- Neal Hefti did some things that fitted in nicely, too.
Oh, yeah, but not very much.
No, Neal was not a very productive
writer during that period of his life. He was too busy playing, still.

And actually, he came up with a lot of ideas and a lot of head things that he put together or helped to put together, where everyone contributed. And some of the best things that were done in any of those pieces were Neal's. But actually, his full arrangements, I think, after The Good Earth and -- I'll name them all -- The Good Earth, Black Orchid and Let It Snow, Let It Snow, and one other, I can't think of what it is, were the only complete things that he brought in.
And the rest of the time, he was always in there, fixing something, changing it, and making some remarkable things happen.
That was his style, in a sense.
You seemed to have trumpet player writers. Shorty did some things.
Oh, yeah, he did a lot of good things for us, yeah.
